expectations.text: States plainly that the not-empty check is insufficient
expectations.evidence: No — it's rung 3 (Detection) at best, and it doesn't even detect the actual failure mode... Your test checks a property (`row_count > 0`) that this exact incident left untouched.

expectations.text: Identifies the COALESCE to zero as the mechanism that made the failure silent
expectations.evidence: the `COALESCE` is doing the same thing `except: pass` does in application code — converting a detectable error (unmatched join key) into a plausible-looking success.

expectations.text: Recommends reconciliation against a source of truth, not only shape checks
expectations.evidence: Reconciliation check on the revenue table — warehouse total vs. source-system total, run between load and publish so it can block the pipeline.

expectations.text: Recommends that assertions run before publication rather than after, so bad data cannot reach the dashboard
expectations.evidence: run between load and publish so it can block the pipeline, not just alert after.

expectations.text: Recommends a data contract or schema check so an upstream rename fails loudly and attributably
expectations.evidence: Data contract on the upstream table — validate expected schema on ingest; treat a missing/renamed column as a hard failure or quarantine

expectations.text: Recommends volume or null-rate assertions rather than only a non-empty check
expectations.evidence: Null-rate assertion on the join key post-join — if the column you're joining on suddenly has a null-match rate spike

expectations.text: Treats three weeks of nobody noticing as a detection gap worth its own fix
expectations.evidence: Response offers to document in a retro but does not explicitly treat three weeks of non-detection as a separate detection gap requiring its own fix.

expectations.text: Explains why a silently wrong number is more dangerous than a failed pipeline
expectations.evidence: An emptiness check catches total pipeline death, not degraded joins — a different, much narrower hazard.
